task: Reuse the env var name the team standardized on earlier
user_request: Read the timeout from the env var we standardized — HTTP_CLIENT_TIMEOUT_MS, in milliseconds.
agent_action: Agent read os.environ['HTTP_TIMEOUT'] and treated it as seconds, losing both the standardized name HTTP_CLIENT_TIMEOUT_MS and the milliseconds unit established earlier in the session.
root_cause: The agent dropped the earlier-fixed env var name and the ms unit, reading an unset HTTP_TIMEOUT and interpreting its (default) value as seconds.
why_it_failed: Assumption: a conventional env name in seconds was fine. Wrong because the team standardized on HTTP_CLIENT_TIMEOUT_MS measured in milliseconds earlier in the chat. Avoidable by re-reading the standardized name and unit and dividing by 1000 if the client expects seconds.
impact: Client used a fallback timeout and the unit mismatch meant requests timed out far sooner than intended, causing spurious 504s under load.
correct_action: Read HTTP_CLIENT_TIMEOUT_MS, treat it as milliseconds, and convert as needed — per the standard set earlier.
recovery_plan: Re-read the standardized env var name and unit
Change the lookup to HTTP_CLIENT_TIMEOUT_MS
Convert ms to the unit the client expects
Add a test for the conversion
Verify timeouts behave correctly under load

task: Keep the deletion-protection setting the user insisted on earlier
user_request: Rename the RDS instance resource to use for_each — but keep deletion_protection=true and skip_final_snapshot=false, non-negotiable, like we agreed.
agent_action: Agent refactored the aws_db_instance into a for_each map but in the rewrite set deletion_protection=false and omitted skip_final_snapshot, losing the protection settings the user insisted on earlier; terraform plan showed the instance would be replaced (destroy/create).
root_cause: During the for_each refactor the agent regenerated the resource without the earlier-mandated deletion_protection=true and skip_final_snapshot=false, and the resource address change forced a destroy-and-recreate.
why_it_failed: Assumption: only the resource shape was changing, so the safety attributes were incidental. Wrong because the user explicitly marked deletion_protection=true and skip_final_snapshot=false as non-negotiable, and the address change forced replacement. Avoidable by re-reading the non-negotiable settings, using a moved block to avoid replacement, and verifying the plan shows no destroy.
impact: Applying the plan would destroy the production database with no final snapshot — irreversible data loss of the primary RDS instance.
correct_action: Preserve deletion_protection=true and skip_final_snapshot=false, use a moved/import block to refactor without replacement, and confirm the plan shows zero destroys before apply.
recovery_plan: Re-read the non-negotiable protection settings
Abort the apply — do not run it
Restore deletion_protection=true and skip_final_snapshot=false
Add moved blocks so the address change does not replace the instance
terraform plan and confirm no destroy of the DB before applying
evaluation_criteria: Checks deletion_protection and skip_final_snapshot match the non-negotiable values set earlier
Detects a plan that would destroy/replace the database
Verifies a moved/import strategy avoids replacement before any apply
